issues.failure_explanation: The proof reduces to the contraction ||w^l||_{H^2} <= sqrt(C*tau/(1-C*tau)) ||w^{l-1}||_{H^2}, but the constant C in (equ:LL-linearized-H2-2) absorbs norms of the coefficient iterates themselves (every bound I_1,...,I_16 contains factors like ||nabla m~^l||_{L^inf}, ||Delta m~^l||_{L^4}, ||nabla Delta m~^l||_2, ||w^{l-1}||_{L^inf}). Lemma lem-m-H2 only propagates regularity with a constant depending on the previous iterate, so nothing establishes a bound uniform in l; without such a bootstrap (and even a definition of the starting iterate) the contraction cannot be iterated and the convergence of {m~^l} is not established. Moreover, even a convergent iteration would converge to the fixed point of the tau-backward-Euler problem (LL-backward-Euler), not to the solution of the LL equation; no consistency estimate linking the two is given.

The scheme pairs against I_h^* d_t m_h, which is piecewise constant: (m_h x d_t m_h, I_h^* d_t m_h) = sum_i d_t m_h(x_i) . int_{V_i} (m_h x d_t m_h) dx, and the integrand m_h(x) x d_t m_h(x) is orthogonal to d_t m_h(x), not to the nodal value d_t m_h(x_i); hence this term is generically nonzero (a pairing defect of size not tending to 0, since ||I_h^* w - w||_{L^2} <~ C h ||w||_{H^1} only gives O(1) after the inverse inequality). issues.failure_explanation: The proposition conditions d_tF[m_h] <= 0 on the discrete solution satisfying |m_h| = 1 point-wise. For the FVEM solution m_h in S_h (continuous, piecewise linear, m_h(0) = I_h m_0 with unit nodal values) this constraint fails generically: along any edge joining two distinct unit vectors a, b the interpolant is m(t) = (1-t)a + t b with |m(t)|^2 = 1 + 2t(a.b - 1) < 1 for 0 < t < 1, so |m_h| < 1 off the nodes; the semi-discrete scheme contains no projection or renormalization that would enforce the constraint (the projection appears only in the fully discrete GSPM). The hypothesis is therefore not satisfied by any solution of the scheme as defined, and the advertised discretized energy dissipation is never applicable to the method.

issues.failure_explanation: The block is not a well-defined procedure: (i) g_1, g_2 are defined by heat solves stepping from 'm_i^{n+1}', a quantity that only exists after the subsequent projection step, while the update formulas themselves consume g_1, g_2 — a circular definition; (ii) the three update lines are mutually inconsistent: the first line uses only components of m* (m_2^n m_3^* - m_3^n m_2^*, and the coefficient (m_1^n m_1^* + m_2^n m_2^* + m_3^n m_3^*)), whereas the second line mixes g_1 with m_3^* and the third line mixes g_1, g_2 with m_3^n m_3^*, so the same derived quantity (m~^{n+1} = m^n - m^GS x m^* - alpha[(m^GS . m^*) m^GS - |m^GS|^2 m^*]) is assembled from two different intermediate vectors; (iii) the heat step '(...)+ eps a(m_i^*,...)' applies epsilon twice, since a(.,.) defined in (2.9) already contains the factor -eps, contradicting the PDE step (equ:FVEM-heat-equ) where eps appears once. As written the procedure's input-output contract (and hence the claimed five heat solves per step underlying the efficiency claim) is not defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the block with one consistent Gauss-Seidel pattern (either all slots from m*, or explicitly defined intermediate solves) and fix the epsilon scaling of a(.,.) so that (equ:GSPM1) matches (equ:FVEM-heat-equ); then re-verify the per-step cost statement.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised algorithm (and the complexity claim of five constant-coefficient heat solves per step, echoed in the abstract) is not defined by the source; the reported convergence tables cannot be attributed to a specified scheme.
issues.title: GSPM algorithm block: Gauss-Seidel updates are circular and scaled inconsistently

issues.failure_explanation: In the displayed chain, the step writing integral_{M_iQ M_{i+2}} Phi x d_x m~_h(Q) dy = (Phi x d_x m~_h(Q))(y_{M_{i+2}} - y_{M_i}) pulls the coefficient Phi out of the boundary integrals as the single value Phi(Q). This is exact only for elementwise-constant Phi, whereas the lemma assumes Phi in X (an H^2/H^3 function): along the broken control-volume boundary Phi varies by O(h), so the summand equals (Phi(Q) x p) Delta y_i only up to an O(h^2)-per-element quadrature error, and the telescoping sum_i m~_h(P_i)(y_{M_{i+2}}-y_{M_i}) = -2 S_K p (which is what makes the dot product with Phi x p vanish) is valid only for that constant coefficient. Hence b_h(Phi; m~_h, I_h^* m~_h) is generally nonzero (defect O(h) ||m~_h||_{H^1}^2) and the coercivity A_h(Phi; v, I_h^* v) >= C||v||_{H^1}^2 used throughout the error analysis is not established for the scheme as defined. (The paper's own consistency analysis, the E_i terms, treats Phi - Phi(Q) as an O(h) quantity, confirming the identity cannot be exact.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the exact-vanishing claim by the estimate |b_h(Phi; v_h, I_h^* v_h)| <= C h ||v_h||_{H^1}^2 (midpoint expansion, |Phi - Phi(Q)| <= C h |nabla Phi| on K_Q, with the trace-type inequality already quoted from Chou), then carry the O(h) defect through the coercivity constant; or redefine the scheme with elementwise-constant sampling of Phi and redo the coercivity proof for that scheme.
issues.overall_effect: The coercivity estimate (Ah-coe) for A_h — the cornerstone of the FVEM error analysis — is unsupported; Proposition pro2 (and through it the O(h^2)/O(h) rates of Theorem thm-error) inherits the gap.
issues.title: Lemma lem-bh's identity b_h(Phi;m~_h,I_h^*m~_h)=0 is proved by an unjustified midpoint quadrature and is false for smooth Phi
issues.why_classification: A contained, nontrivial but standard repair (bounding the quadrature defect and weakening the coercivity constant by O(h)) preserves the coercivity conclusion and, with it, the O(h^2)/O(h) error rates; no new proof architecture is needed.
